enonce: Choisis le mot qui complète chaque phrase.

questions.intitule: *The HR department is worried about staff ......, which has dropped this winter.*
*The high level of ...... in the town makes it easy to recruit workers.*
*The board meeting will be ...... on the fifth floor.*
*Did you receive the ...... for Friday's meeting?*
*After a short lunch break, the workshop will ...... at 2 p.m.*

indices: Regarde la nature du mot attendu, puis le sens.
correction: 1. *attendance* a baissé (*dropped*) : c'est inquiétant. 2. *the level of* + nom : *unemployment*. 3. passif : *will be held*. 4. réunion à venir : *agenda*. 5. reprise après la pause : *resume*.

enonce: Choisis le mot qui complète chaque phrase.

questions.intitule: *All new staff must ...... in at the main entrance.*
*Ms. Ito has been ...... head of the Tokyo branch.*
*Three ...... were invited for a second interview.*
*The company plans to ...... its workforce by 10% next year.*
*Our contract is ...... for both parties.*
*Part-time workers are not ...... for the annual bonus.*

indices: *lay* demande la particule *off* ; *retire* et *resign* parlent d'une personne qui part.
correction: 1. *must clock in*. 2. *has been appointed* (passif). 3. personnes invitées : *applicants*. 4. *reduce its workforce by 10%* (réduire ses effectifs) ; *lay* sans *off* n'a pas ce sens. 5. *a binding contract*. 6. *eligible for*.

enonce: Choisis le mot qui complète chaque phrase. Attention, certains pièges sont plus fins.

questions.intitule: *Ms. Lopez ...... the meeting because the director was ill.*
*The ...... of the new manager will be announced on Monday.*
*We are pleased to offer you the ...... of sales assistant.*
*Please let us know ...... you can attend the training session.*
*The trainees are looking forward ...... the factory next week.*
*...... the heavy snow, all employees came to work.*

correction: 1. *chaired* = a présidé. 2. *The ... of* → nom : *appointment*. 3. *the position of sales assistant* = le poste de. 4. *let us know whether* = dites-nous si. 5. *look forward to* + -ing. 6. *Despite* + nom (*the heavy snow*).

titre: Partie 6 : une invitation à un entretien
enonce:
Lis l'e-mail, puis complète chaque trou.

> **From** : Laura Benson, HR Manager, Corvex Logistics
> **To** : Daniel Okafor
> **Subject** : Your application
>
> Dear Mr. Okafor,
>
> Thank you for your application for the (1) ...... of warehouse supervisor. We were impressed by your experience, and you are now on our (2) ....... We would like to meet you next Tuesday or Wednesday, (3) ...... .
> Before the interview, could you (4) ...... the names of two former employers who can give you a reference?
>
> I look forward (5) ...... you.
>
> Kind regards,
> Laura Benson

choix: whichever is more convenient for you

indices: *on our ...* : après un possessif, il faut un nom.
correction: (1) *the position of* = le poste de. (2) *on our shortlist* (nom). (3) *whichever is more convenient for you* = le jour qui vous arrange le mieux ; les autres choix n'ont pas de sens ici. (4) *provide the names* = fournir. (5) *I look forward to meeting you*.

enonce:
Lis la note, puis complète chaque trou.

> **MEMO**
> **To** : All staff
> **From** : Events committee
>
> This year's staff (1) ...... will take place on Friday 14 June. We will spend the day at Lake Arden, where a picnic lunch will be (2) ....... The bus will leave the office at 9 a.m. (3) ......, anyone who prefers to drive can meet us at the lake.
> Please tell Mia Clark (4) ...... you will join us by 31 May. The (5) ...... of the day will be posted on the noticeboard next week.
correction: (1) *staff outing* = sortie du personnel. (2) *will be provided* (passif). (3) *Alternatively* propose une autre solution (venir en voiture). (4) *tell her whether* = dire si. (5) *the schedule of the day* = le programme ; les *minutes* sont un compte-rendu de réunion.

enonce:
Lis l'annonce, puis réponds.

> **Weekend receptionist wanted - Harbour View Hotel**
> We are looking for a friendly receptionist to work Saturdays and Sundays (16 hours per week). Experience in a hotel is an advantage but not required: full training will be given. The position is paid $15 per hour, and staff meals are included.
> To apply, send your résumé to jobs@harbourview.com before 30 April. Shortlisted candidates will be interviewed in the first week of May.

questions.intitule: How many hours per week is the job?
What is said about experience?
choix: It is useful but not necessary.
At least two years are needed.

questions.intitule: What benefit is mentioned?
What will happen in early May?

indices: *an advantage but not required* = un plus, mais pas obligatoire.
correction: 1. *16 hours per week*. 2. *an advantage but not required*. 3. *staff meals are included*. 4. *Shortlisted candidates will be interviewed in the first week of May*.

titre: Partie 7 : un e-mail et un planning
enonce:
Lis les deux documents, puis réponds.

**Document 1 : e-mail**

> **From** : Ken Adams, Office Manager
> **To** : Sales team
> **Date** : Monday 3 March
>
> Hi all,
> The sales training planned for Wednesday has been postponed by one day because the trainer's flight was cancelled. The session will be held in Room 4 instead of Room 2, which is being painted. Lunch will be provided.
> Ken

**Document 2 : planning des salles**

| Day | Room 2 | Room 4 |
|---|---|---|
| Wednesday 5 March | closed (painting) | IT workshop |
| Thursday 6 March | closed (painting) | free |
| Friday 7 March | board meeting | client visit |

questions.intitule: Why was the training postponed?
On what day will the training take place?
Why can't the session take place in Room 2?
choix: It is booked for a board meeting.

questions.intitule: What is NOT mentioned about the training?

indices: *postponed by one day* : décalé d'un jour.
Croise l'e-mail avec le planning : le jeudi, la salle 4 est libre.
correction: 1. *the trainer's flight was cancelled*. 2. Mercredi + un jour = **jeudi 6 mars**, et la salle 4 est libre ce jour-là. 3. *Room 2, which is being painted*. 4. Le nom du formateur n'est jamais donné.

enonce:
Lis les trois documents, puis réponds.

**Document 1 : compte-rendu**

> **Minutes - Greenfield Sports Centre committee - 2 April**
> Present: Tom Reyes, Alice Moreau, Sam Patel. Absent: Nina Lee.
> Members of the public have complained that the swimming pool closes too early. Tom Reyes said the budget does not allow more lifeguards. Alice Moreau suggested hiring sports-science students part-time, so the pool can stay open later and the students can gain experience. Sam Patel agreed to write a job advertisement for the university website.
> Next meeting: 16 April.

**Document 2 : annonce**

> **Students: work at Greenfield Sports Centre!**
> We are taking on four lifeguards for evening shifts (6 p.m. - 9 p.m., three evenings a week). Applicants must be studying sports science and hold a lifesaving certificate. Send your résumé to Nina Lee, Centre Manager, at nlee@greenfield.org.

**Document 3 : e-mail**

> **To** : Sam Patel
> **From** : Nina Lee
> **Date** : 15 April
> Sam, thanks for the advert: we've received 30 applications! Could you help me choose the best candidates? I'm busy at the reception desk today, but we can compare our lists at the committee meeting.
> Nina

questions.intitule: Why does the committee want to hire students?
choix: To keep the pool open later

questions.intitule: Who most likely wrote the advertisement?
Who is Nina Lee?
What is NOT stated about the job?
What will happen on the day after the e-mail?
How many lifeguards does the centre want to take on?

indices: Cherche dans le compte-rendu qui s'est proposé pour rédiger l'annonce.
E-mail du 15 avril ; prochaine réunion le 16 avril.
correction: 1. *so the pool can stay open later*. 2. *Sam Patel agreed to write a job advertisement*, et Nina le remercie pour l'annonce. 3. *Nina Lee, Centre Manager*. 4. Horaires, études et certificat sont donnés ; le salaire, non. 5. E-mail le 15 avril, réunion le **16 avril** (*we can compare our lists at the committee meeting*). 6. *four lifeguards*.

titre: Partie 2 sur papier : réunions et RH
enonce: Voici des questions de partie 2, écrites. Choisis la réponse logique.

questions.intitule: *Who is going to chair the meeting tomorrow?*
*Has the agenda been sent out yet?*
choix: The agent is on the phone.

questions.intitule: *Why don't we postpone the training until May?*
*Where should I send my résumé?*
*You'll be at the retirement party, won't you?*
choix: The party is a political group.
Of course, I wouldn't miss it.

correction: 1. *Who* → une personne. 2. *yet* → oui ou non + info. 3. *Why don't we...?* = proposition : on l'accepte ou on la refuse. 4. *Where* → un lieu ou un service. 5. *won't you?* attend une confirmation.

titre: Partie 3 sur papier : une réunion déplacée
enonce:
Lis la transcription, puis réponds.

> **Man** : Hi Emma, quick question: the team meeting is still at 9 tomorrow, right?
> **Woman** : Actually, no. It's been moved to 10. Several people are coming back from the trade fair tonight, and their train arrives very late.
> **Man** : Ah, that makes sense. I'll tell the new intern, she starts tomorrow.
> **Woman** : Great. And remind her it's important: we'll be discussing the summer schedule, so nobody should skip it.

questions.intitule: What time will the meeting start?
Why was the time changed?
choix: Some colleagues will return late the night before.

questions.intitule: What does the woman mean by "nobody should skip it"?
choix: Everyone should come to the meeting.

questions.intitule: What will the man do?

indices: *to skip* = sauter, ne pas aller à.
correction: 1. *It's been moved to 10*. 2. *Several people are coming back from the trade fair tonight, and their train arrives very late*. 3. *skip* = ne pas venir : tout le monde doit être présent. 4. *I'll tell the new intern*.

enonce: Pour chaque phrase, choisis pourquoi la réponse proposée est **fausse**.

questions.intitule: *The meeting will be take place in Room C.* Pourquoi est-ce faux ?
choix: *take place* ne se met pas au passif

questions.intitule: *Have you seen the minutes of next week's meeting?* Pourquoi est-ce bizarre ?
choix: Les *minutes* sont rédigées après une réunion

questions.intitule: *I look forward to meet you.* Pourquoi est-ce faux ?
choix: Après *look forward to*, il faut un verbe en -ing

questions.intitule: *Staff absenteeism is very low, so the director is worried.* Pourquoi est-ce illogique ?
choix: Un absentéisme bas est une bonne nouvelle

indices: Ce sont les pièges du mini test.
correction: 1. On dit *will take place* ou *will be held*. 2. Pour une réunion à venir : *the agenda*. 3. *look forward to meeting you*. 4. Si la direction s'inquiète, c'est que la **présence** (*attendance*) est basse.

questions.intitule: le chômage
l'absentéisme
dès que possible (formule polie, 4 mots : *at your earliest ...*)
au nom de (la bibliothèque)
la charge de travail
la liste des candidats retenus

enonce: Tu as reçu l'e-mail de l'exercice « Partie 6 : une invitation à un entretien ». Rédige une réponse de 3 ou 4 phrases : remercie, choisis un jour, dis que tu fournis tes références.

questions.intitule: Ta réponse
questions.reponse:
Exemple :

*Dear Ms. Benson,*

*Thank you for your e-mail and for shortlisting me. Wednesday would be the most convenient day for me, ideally in the morning. Please find attached the contact details of two former employers who can provide a reference. I look forward to meeting you.*

*Kind regards,*
*Daniel Okafor*

indices: Termine par *I look forward to meeting you*.
correction: À vérifier : remerciement (*Thank you for...*), choix d'un jour (*Wednesday would suit me*), références (*Please find attached...*), formule finale avec *look forward to* + -ing.
